# Page header

The top of a page inside the shell: a breadcrumb, the title, a description, actions, a row of facts and optional tabs.

Status: Stable. Semantic versioning applies: nothing breaks without a deprecation first.

Where am I, what is this, what can I do. Breadcrumbs sit above the title because they are navigation you can click back along — not an eyebrow pre-announcing the heading. Actions wrap below the title on a narrow screen rather than hiding in an overflow menu: the primary action of a page is the last thing that should cost an extra click.

## Usage

### When to use

- Saying where the reader is, what the page is and what they can do on it.
- Short facts about the object, such as status, owner and last update, through meta.
- Tabs that switch views of the page, on the header’s bottom edge.

### When not to

- A title for a section inside a page. Use [SectionHeader](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-layout-container--overview.md).
- A title that is the whole point of the screen, such as an onboarding panel. Use [Display](https://demogar.github.io/molaui/md/components-typography-display--overview.md).

### Do and don’t

- Do: Keep the page’s main action in actions, where it wraps under the title on a narrow screen.
- Don’t: Hide the main action in an overflow menu.

### Content

- The title is the object’s name or the collection’s: “Runs”, “Support triage”.
- The description says what the page holds in one sentence.
- Meta items are short facts, not sentences: “Updated 12s ago”, “Retention 30 days”.

## Anatomy

The root carries `data-slot="page-header"`; each part carries its `data-part`.

1. Header (`[data-slot="page-header"]`): Closes on a keyline, unless tabs sit at its foot.
2. Title (`[data-part="title"]`): The page’s one h1.
3. Description (`[data-part="description"]`): One sentence on what the page is for.
4. Actions (`[data-part="actions"]`): The page’s actions. They wrap below the title on a narrow screen rather than hide in a menu.
5. Meta (`[data-part="meta"]`): Status, owner and dates, as a list divided by keylines.

## API

### `PageHeader` (component)

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `breadcrumb` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `meta` | `ReactNode[]` |  |  |
| `tabs` | `ReactNode` |  | A Tabs list. Sits on the header's bottom edge so the active tab cuts into it. |

`className`, `ref`, `id` and the other DOM props go to `<header data-slot="page-header">`.

Types: `PageHeaderProps`

## Accessibility

Nothing in it takes focus, so there is no keyboard table.

### Mola handles

- Renders the title as the page's `h1`.
- Renders `meta` as a list, so a screen reader says how many facts there are.

### You handle

- Use one page header per page, so the page has one `h1`.
- Pass a breadcrumb that is its own named navigation.

### Testing status

- Automated, jsdom: each of its 2 stories is rendered and checked with axe on every pull request.
- Automated, browser: every story is checked in Chromium with axe, colour contrast included, in both themes, and for overflow at 390px.
- Keyboard in unit tests: not applicable.
- Screen readers: not yet tested by hand.
